recognize_zh: 抹片背景中散在淡紫藍色、雲霧狀無結構的細胞外沉積物（箭頭），為冷球蛋白；自動血球計數器把這些沉積物誤判為血小板，B 圖可見儀器血小板數突然升到約 500×10³/µL，但人工計數始終偏低。
features: Extracellular pale lilac-blue, amorphous, cloud-like or fluffy deposits in the smear background (arrows)
Deposits lack granules, nuclei or defined membranes, distinguishing them from platelets
Deformed red cells with indentations or folding (arrowheads) and an occasional crenated red cell
True platelets are scarce in this field
Panel B graph: analyzer-derived platelet count spikes to ~500 × 10^3/µL around days 5–9 while manual counts remain below ~25 × 10^3/µL
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows extracellular, pale lilac-blue, amorphous cloud-like deposits scattered between red cells, consistent with precipitated cryoglobulin, together with deformed red cells and very few true platelets. The accompanying graph shows a discrepancy in which the automated analyzer platelet count rises abruptly to about 500 × 10^3/µL while manual platelet counts remain severely low. This indicates that cryoglobulin particles were counted as platelets, producing pseudo-recovery. Findings are consistent with cryoglobulins causing spurious platelet counts in a patient with mantle cell lymphoma after chemoimmunotherapy; warmed-sample recount and manual smear review are recommended.

ddx.vs: Recovered platelets are discrete granular fragments on the smear with concordant manual counts, whereas here the smear shows amorphous deposits and manual counts stay low.

ddx.dx: Red cell or leukocyte fragments counted as platelets
ddx.vs: Fragments (schistocytes, microspherocytes, blast cytoplasm) have red cell color or cellular structure, unlike featureless pale blue cloud-like material.
Platelet clumps contain granular platelets and fibrin forms fibrillar strands, not homogeneous amorphous blotches.
Stain precipitate is dark purple and granular and lies on top of cells, whereas cryoglobulin is pale, smooth and extracellular and disappears when the sample is warmed.
